headline: The Statue of Unity's home district, a mega-monument at the edge of deep tribal forest country.
overview:
Narmada district runs on a striking contrast. On its river-facing edge stands India's biggest tourism project of the last decade: the 182-metre Statue of Unity at Ekta Nagar (formerly Kevadia), ringed by the Sardar Sarovar dam, ticketed gardens, a zoological park, cruise jetties and a purpose-built railway station. Forty minutes south and east, the district turns into something entirely different, the 600 km² Shoolpaneshwar sanctuary's hill forests, monsoon waterfalls at Zarwani and Ninai, the princely leftovers of Rajpipla, and a tribal heartland whose great festival at Devmogra draws half a million Vasava and Bhil devotees each spring.

Most visitors come for the statue and leave having seen only the campus. The district rewards those who stay a second day: rafting below the dam, the Datta pilgrimage at Garudeshwar, the Swaminarayan complex at Poicha, palace-and-bazaar Rajpipla, and, in season, the eastern belt's falls and forest campsites. Ekta Nagar's infrastructure is the best in the region; beyond Rajpipla, expect rural roads, thin signal and the forest department as your host.

October to February is the comfortable season and the SoU peak; monsoon brings the dam releases, full waterfalls and green hills at the price of heat-free but humid days.

hubs.name: Ekta Nagar (Kevadia)
hubs.notes: SoU base town: hotels, e-buses, the campus circuit

hubs.name: Ekta Nagar railway station
hubs.notes: Direct trains from Ahmedabad, Mumbai and other cities; itself built as a showcase

hubs.name: Rajpipla
hubs.notes: District headquarters; civil hospital, markets, palace heritage

hubs.name: Dediapada
hubs.notes: Gateway to the eastern forest belt and Shoolpaneshwar sanctuary

hubs.name: Vadodara airport
hubs.notes: ~90 km from Ekta Nagar, the practical airport

getting_there.road: Ekta Nagar is ~90 km from Vadodara and ~85 km from Bharuch on excellent highways; Rajpipla sits 25 km west of the campus. Dediapada and the eastern belt connect via the Rajpipla–Sagbara corridor. Buses run from Vadodara, Bharuch and Surat; taxis are plentiful on the SoU routes.
getting_there.rail: Ekta Nagar station has direct services from Ahmedabad, Mumbai and other cities timed for SoU tourism; Ankleshwar and Bharuch junctions cover the west of the district.
getting_there.air: Vadodara (~90 km) is the practical airport; Surat and Ahmedabad (~200 km) also work.

local_transport: Within the SoU campus, ticketed e-buses and shuttles do the moving; autos and taxis cover Ekta Nagar town and Rajpipla. Beyond Rajpipla and Dediapada, shared jeeps and own transport are the reality, book return taxis for the eastern belt, and expect no app cabs anywhere in the district.

weather_by_month.notes: Waterfalls wake up; dam releases possible
Best month for Zarwani/Ninai and dam spectacle

best_season: October–February for the Statue of Unity and general touring (book ahead for Diwali and Christmas–New Year weeks); July–September for waterfalls, dam releases and the green Shoolpaneshwar belt; the Devmogra fair lands in Feb–Mar. April–June is hot, campus mornings and evenings only.

emergency.police: 112 (national emergency); Ekta Nagar (Kevadia), Rajpipla, Garudeshwar, Dediapada and Sagbara police stations
hospitals: Ekta Nagar area medical facilities and first-aid posts
emergency.forest_dept: Shoolpaneshwar division; check posts at Thawadia (Ekta Nagar side) and the Dediapada ranges handle sanctuary entry

tips: The entire SoU campus closes on Mondays, build itineraries around it
Book viewing-gallery and safari slots online days ahead for weekends and holiday weeks
Fuel up at Rajpipla or Ekta Nagar before the eastern belt; Dediapada is the last dependable stop
Forest campsites (Zarwani, Sagai, Khalwani) book via the official eco-tourism portal, not OTAs
Gujarat is a dry state, no alcohol is sold anywhere in the district
